paper.title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents
paper.central_claim: Large pretrained language models contain actionable knowledge for diverse high-level activities without additional domain training; semantic action translation, dynamic example retrieval and interleaved trajectory correction can make their plans executable in embodied environments.

patterns/main/observe_act_interface.md: - **Extra tools are optional and checked per backbone.** Tools are added beside primitives rather than replacing them, harness parse/coordinate/feedback correctness is verified before comparison, and effects are reported per model: optional hybrid tools raise the strongest model 82.3 -> 85.7 SR at 0.59x calls, while imposed waypoints lift weak models (5 -> 43 SR) and move strong ones by <=2 points (2607.26148#s2, 2608.03327#s1).

- **E01 (ablation, common_practice).** Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.

- **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.

- **E03 (ablation, common_practice).** Report the harness or tool effect under at least two backbones of different strength. Several read papers find that tools and imposed structure help weak models and are neutral or harmful for strong ones. A gain measured on the teacher therefore does not predict the gain for a compact student. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness component or tool helps in general, or that a teacher-measured tool value will carry to a student.

- **E05 (metric, common_practice).** Report cost alongside success: model calls, input and output tokens, wall-clock or per-call latency, and USD per episode or per solved task, including failed trials. Harnesses with similar pass rates can differ about 40x in tokens per solved task. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.

- **E06 (dataset, common_practice).** For a VLN-CE harness, report SR, SPL, OSR and NE on R2R-CE val_unseen, either on the shared 100-episode zero-shot subset or the full split. State which one, and do not mix subset results with full-split numbers of trained methods as if they were matched. — _applies when_ an empirical claim about a zero-shot or harness-based VLN-CE / ObjectNav agent.

- **E08 (reproducibility, common_practice).** State contamination and development-overlap caveats. Frontier 'zero-shot' describes how the model was used, not what it was trained on. Disclose whether the evaluation tasks were used during harness development, and whether ablations ran under a privileged action space that is not comparable to the benchmark protocol. — _applies when_ a benchmark claim by a frontier-model harness, or ablations run under non-standard execution.

- **E16 (metric, common_practice).** Break failures down by endpoint as well as SR: never reached vs reached but wrong stop (the OSR-SR gap), false completion declarations, stuck or no-progress runs, and per-task repeat patterns. Stopping is the dominant residual failure in the read navigation papers. — _applies when_ an embodied navigation or manipulation agent's success claim, especially one that adds a stop or completion check.

- **E20 (other, common_practice).** State the depth assumption behind depth-based perception tools (pixel depth queries, back-projection, stop checks): whether depth is metric and calibrated, and whether behaviour under non-metric or scene-dependent depth was tested. — _applies when_ a harness whose tools or gates convert depth readings into distances, targets or stop decisions.

- **E22 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Compare interfaces and harnesses at a matched interaction budget: the same caps on LLM calls, turns, wall-clock time and GPU. Disclose any asymmetry, such as uncapped turns or extra compute for tool runs, because budget endings drive many success differences. — _applies when_ a comparison between harnesses, interfaces or tool bundles with the model fixed.

research/reference/researchstudio-15-31/: - **Run an ablation that isolates the conditioning signal — comparing instruction, format, or retrieval conditioning against the same multitask training without it — to prove the gain comes from conditioning and not merely from broader exposure.** _(source: both)_

- **Provide a contamination or data-overlap analysis between the adaptation tasks and the held-out evaluation set before any genuine held-out or zero-shot generalization claim is accepted.** _(source: both)_

- **Compare against the obvious cheaper alternative — longer input context, nearest-neighbor lookup, or plain multitask fine-tuning — so the unique value of the conditioning or retrieval is established rather than assumed.** _(source: reject_reviews)_

- **Justify each component of a multi-module conditioning pipeline with ablations that isolate its contribution; shallow ablations over interacting components are treated as insufficient.** _(source: both)_
- **Demonstrate that the recipe is generic across multiple tasks or domains and explain how the conditioning signal is obtained without a manual, per-task search.** _(source: reject_reviews)_

- **Characterize sensitivity to the quality and coverage of the conditioning source — the demonstration or retrieval database — and to the distributional gap between that source and the test domain.** _(source: both)_
- **Report the cost of the added structure — token and API budget, number of model or solver calls, and solver latency — rather than only end-task accuracy.** _(source: both)_

- **Provide ablations that isolate each component's marginal contribution, and especially show the claimed load-bearing step is what drives the gains rather than extra data or compute.** _(source: both)_
- **Disclose the exact prompts and implementation details so the decomposed pipeline is reproducible and the results are not suspected prompt-engineering artifacts.** _(source: both)_
- **Demonstrate generalization beyond a single narrow benchmark or domain, ideally with cross-domain or real-world tasks rather than templates specific to one dataset.** _(source: both)_
- **Compare fairly against simpler unified or end-to-end baselines and against concurrent decomposition methods, clarifying precisely what is novel relative to them.** _(source: both)_

- **Justify that the decomposition targets a genuine structural bottleneck — ideally evidenced by an empirical diagnostic linking a sub-task to the final outcome — instead of imposing structure for its own sake.** _(source: both)_

signatures.object: Free-form LLM action output versus executable semantic actions
signatures.information: High-level task, admissible action bank, pretrained sentence embeddings; no current scene observations.
signatures.operation: Embed generated step; rank legal action strings using similarity and LM likelihood; replace free-form step and append translated step to the next planning context.
signatures.conditions: 42 atomic actions, allowed object arguments and sufficient semantic embedding similarity.
signatures.feedback: Translated previous actions, not environmental success/failure.
signatures.selection_rule/data: Candidate samples selected by similarity plus beta-scaled mean log probability; epsilon/empty-generation stopping; development settings in Appendix A.1.
signatures.persistence: Static harness design and per-episode context; no accepted cross-task optimizer change is claimed.
signatures.later_use: Fixed components are reused on tasks; within-episode context is read by subsequent planner calls. This is not measured retained self-improvement.
signatures.failure_boundary: Compounded commands, incomplete environment vocabulary and early stopping can preserve validity while losing task correctness.

signatures.object: Fixed few-shot example versus task-adaptive retrieval
signatures.information: 204 demonstration task names and scripts, frozen embedding similarity; 88 task-name evaluation set.
signatures.operation: Retrieve a nearby demonstration and condition the planner on it.
signatures.output: Task-specific example in a common task-to-program prompt.
signatures.conditions: Relevant retrievable reference tasks; no claim of online library mining.
signatures.selection_rule/data: Nearest task embedding; global sampling choices ranked by LCS and executability.
signatures.persistence: Static harness design and per-episode context; no accepted cross-task optimizer change is claimed.
signatures.later_use: Fixed components are reused on tasks; within-episode context is read by subsequent planner calls. This is not measured retained self-improvement.
signatures.claimed_effect: Improve extraction of executable multi-step programs.
signatures.failure_boundary: Does not establish unseen-category transfer or contamination-free independent tuning.

gap.author_gap: Existing LLM knowledge extraction and language grounding do not yield executable plans for diverse high-level human activities without additional training.
gap.checked_gap: Same-model vanilla generations are often semantically plausible but not executable; projection sharply improves executability while reducing human correctness. The residual is executable-and-correct planning, not merely legal syntax.

lineage/closest_adjacent.method: VirtualHome human scripts and supervised instruction-to-program LSTM; generic pretrained LM prompting.
lineage/closest_adjacent.source_verification: Paper-reported lineage only for the original VirtualHome/LSTM work; its separate primary text and exact original version were not in the fixed input. No claim of exhaustive priority verification.

gap.residue: Free-form world knowledge does not automatically obey an embodied action vocabulary or preconditions.
gap.stakes: An apparently correct plan cannot be acted on; a merely executable short plan can fail the intended activity.
gap.method_response: Translate to admissible actions, retrieve task-relevant examples and interleave corrected actions into generation.
gap.remaining_gap: No environmental observation/feedback, no physical low-level controller validation, and a substantial correctness/executability tradeoff.
unresolved: Exact independent source versions/priority of prior supervised methods are not fixed here.
Hyperparameter-selection versus final-test independence is not established.

claims.text: Large pretrained language models contain actionable knowledge for diverse high-level activities without additional domain training; semantic action translation, dynamic example retrieval and interleaved trajectory correction can make their plans executable in embodied environments.
claims.setting: Codex12B/GPT-3 175B; 88 activity names, seven VirtualHome scenes; 47,522 allowed action strings.
claims.baseline/control: Vanilla generation; Table 2 component removals; fine-tuned GPT-3 baseline separately.
claims.selection_vs_test: 204 reference tasks; best sampled configuration selected using LCS+executability, independent validation split not established.
claims.result/denominator: Codex executable18.07→78.57%; correctness64.87→54.88%. GPT-3 executable7.79→73.05%; correctness77.86→66.13%. Correctness judged by ten annotators; mean/SEM.
claims.counterevidence: Executable is not equivalent to correct; no observation feedback, and pretrained exposure is unauditable.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong evidence for improving static program executability in this simulator interface, not general autonomous embodied success.

claims.text: Extracted plans contain actionable knowledge rather than merely reproducing valid syntax.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same selected plan outputs, not new independent online test.
claims.result/denominator: Joint correct/executable analysis uses ≥70% annotator approval; human joint reference65.91%.
claims.counterevidence: Some correctness is lost during projection; vocabulary expressivity and early stops remain.
claims.allowed_conclusion: There is a measurable but incomplete bridge from text knowledge to executable activities.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported static VirtualHome program executability rises substantially through translation/retrieval/interleaving on the evaluated activity set; the evidence does not establish observation-conditioned closed-loop robot task success.
unresolved: Primary-source historical closest-neighbor version checks beyond M001.
Pretraining overlap and actual inference cost.
assessment.reproduction: No reproduction or paper-code execution was performed.

G.reason: A concrete executable-versus-plausible bottleneck and observed cost are documented; the closest supervised comparison is explicitly crude and its independent source/split is not fixed.

M.reason: Translation and retrieved conditioning target a real interface mismatch with reconstructible predictions; embedding similarity need not preserve task semantics and ignores scene state.

X.reason: Static generation/translation/retrieval/stopping is reconstructible with ablations and explicit boundaries; no retained loop is required. Scope remains a semantic action interface rather than a full environmental feedback controller.

measurement.reason: Executability and human semantic correctness have explicit checks and a joint criterion, but are static proxies rather than environment-observed closed-loop completion.

causality.reason: Fixed-backbone leave-one-out tests across two planners support mechanism attribution; outcome-driven configuration selection and unmatched inference costs prevent a fully controlled causal claim.

holdout.reason: 88 activity names are separated from 204 demonstrations, yet the best runs are selected on evaluation-style metrics without a clearly separate post-selection test; model-pretraining overlap is unknown.

statistics.reason: Ten-annotator SEM and multiple prompt examples quantify parts of uncertainty, but do not supply repeated independent policy trials or CIs for executability and its failures.

cost.reason: Precomputation and sampling structure are reported, giving limited computational visibility, but no realized episode/solved-task latency, token or financial accounting. Complete Section 4/Appendix A.1 search found grids rather than a matched actual-cost comparison.
